items.stem: Why are story points used instead of direct hour estimates in many agile teams?

options.text: Relative sizing is often more reliable than absolute time guesses
options.rationale: Correct: people compare sizes better than they predict exact durations.

options.text: Story points convert directly into hours
options.rationale: They deliberately avoid a fixed hour conversion.

options.text: Hours are never used anywhere in agile
options.rationale: Hours can appear, e.g. in task breakdowns; the point is relative sizing at story level.
No estimate guarantees delivery; they aid forecasting.

items.explanation: Correct: people compare sizes better than they predict exact durations.

items.stem: Which statements about velocity are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It is best used to forecast delivery as a range
options.rationale: Correct: velocity informs probabilistic forecasts, not exact dates.

options.text: It is specific to a given team and context
options.rationale: Correct: velocity is not comparable across different teams.

options.text: It should be used as a productivity target to push teams
options.rationale: Using velocity as a target invites gaming and estimate inflation.

options.text: It converts points into guaranteed calendar dates
options.rationale: Velocity supports forecasts with uncertainty, not guarantees.

items.explanation: Correct: velocity informs probabilistic forecasts, not exact dates.

items.stem: Early in a project, stakeholders demand a single exact completion date. What is the most honest response?

options.text: Provide a range and refine it as uncertainty decreases
options.rationale: Correct: the cone of uncertainty is widest early, so a range is honest.

options.text: Commit to a precise date to look confident
options.rationale: False precision misleads stakeholders and sets up failure.

options.text: Refuse to give any information at all
options.rationale: A reasoned range is both possible and useful.

options.text: Promise the earliest date anyone mentions
options.rationale: Anchoring to an optimistic date ignores real uncertainty.

items.explanation: Correct: the cone of uncertainty is widest early, so a range is honest.
